top_choice_rationale: P001 awards Mircea Cărtărescu alone, with the citation centred on his prose project. On public knowledge of Blinding (the first volume of the Orbitor trilogy) and Solenoid, his is a distinctive voice. Memory, the body, dream and cosmology are built into large recursive structures, so the formal ambition lies in architecture as well as imagery. That supports a claim of sustained imaginative and intellectual depth across a body of work under the common criteria. The citation should credit the prose project and name its cumulative architecture, with the poetry only as the origin of the sentence-level attention, because poetry coverage in translation is thinnest. I judge him through translation and secondary description. I have not read the originals, and I cannot confirm whether the later long works enlarge the project or restate its motifs. Adonis remains a very strong alternative, whose case is harder to verify without Arabic-language expert accounts. That is a gap in the committee's evidence, not a verdict against his work. The unanimity of round-1 and round-2 support is not evidence of merit and I have not counted it as such. Nothing in the supplied evidence justifies preferring no award (P000) over a laureate, so P000 ranks second.
